description: Neutrality claims register. Maps each qualified neutrality wording used in public copy to its substantiating control, CI test IDs, external-evidence IDs and approver/expiry; and records the versioned proposition-selection rationale + scoring spec, bound to the built-dataset proposition manifest. Enforced by scripts/check-neutrality-claims.mjs (the claims/copy arm of the neutrality lint) and wired into the compliance CI groups. See also docs/claims-register.md (prose) and apps/web/src/lib/content/MethodologyContent.svelte (the public surface, rendered by the /methodology route and by the in-flow document dialog).

claims.wording: How2Vote never suggests who to put first
claims.substantiatingControl: Comparison is shown as evidence only; the plan builder starts from a blank ballot (apps/web/src/lib/plan.ts) with no preselection or ranking; BallotRow.svelte styles every row identically so no candidate is crowned. Enforced by content.server.test.ts (routes never touch the scoring engine) and the neutrality-claims banned-phrase scan.

claims.wording: It describes the party, not any individual candidate's personal views
claims.substantiatingControl: Scores are party-level averages of recorded parliamentary voting (methodology 'From members to parties'); a candidate with no personal record is shown against their party's record, never their own inferred view. Enforced by the neutrality-claims methodology-binding check.

A party or candidate with no member on the record for an issue has no position; NO_DATA is carried through scoring so a missing record earns and risks nothing rather than being imputed (packages/engine scoring; methodology 'From members to parties').

claims.wording: candidates are never ranked by score, only ever shown in official ballot order
claims.substantiatingControl: Candidates are rendered in official AEC ballot order (packages/engine ballot.ts), never sorted by alignment; the monochrome-palette neutrality lint (apps/web/scripts/neutrality-check.mjs) additionally prevents any hue reading as a winner. Enforced by the neutrality-claims methodology-binding check + content.server.test.ts.

propositionSelection.rationale: The propositions are selected from They Vote For You policies to span the parliamentary term; choosing and wording them is an editorial judgement, and each proposition links to the divisions behind it so a reader can check the record. Selection aims for coverage across policy areas and across the term rather than issue prominence, salience or any party's advantage; no proposition is included or excluded to steer a result. Each proposition states a concrete, contestable policy action alongside the genuine competing interest it trades off against, so that agreeing and disagreeing are equally reasonable positions rather than a foregone conclusion; the wording never asserts a particular outcome. The upcoming-election comparison additionally draws its propositions from policies the current Parliament has actually divided on, so the set reflects live parliamentary activity rather than any party's advantage.

scoringSpec.scale: Each party position and each user answer sits on a five-point scale (1 strongly disagree … 5 strongly agree); skips count for nothing.
scoringSpec.banding: A party's plain-average agreement figure (0-100) is placed on the five-point scale by dividing 0-100 into five equal bands (0-20 → 1 … 80-100 → 5).
scoringSpec.distance: d = |party − you|, a whole number 0 (identical) … 4 (opposite ends).

pointsAtStake.extremelyImportant: ×10 multiplier on a strong answer: max(0, 40 − 10d)

scoringSpec.overallMatch: match % = round( points earned ÷ points possible × 100 ); merged/renamed parties combine raw earned + possible points before the percentage; a party with no scorable question in common shows as no data rather than 0%.
scoringSpec.noData: A party or candidate with no recorded position on an issue has no position on it — never imputed.
scoringSpec.displayOrder: Party scores are placed beside candidates in official ballot order; nothing is ranked or crowned by score.

pageWording: The propositions are selected from They Vote For You policies to span the parliamentary term; choosing and wording them is an editorial judgement
